pr_body:
### What

Add `--dry-run` flag for `gh pr create` so it can provide a summary of what will be done rather than creating the PR.
`--dry-run` in conjunction with `--web` is not supported

### Why

This can help with knowing what the `gh pr create` will do rather than using it directly. This feature will allow consumers to leverage their workflows to test their changes without writing anything.

### Issues

Closes https://github.com/cli/cli/issues/8375

issue_context.title: Add a dry-run flag to `gh pr create`
issue_context.body:
### Describe the feature or problem you’d like to solve

I can test my scripts without the need to use echos by flags.

### Proposed solution

How will it benefit CLI and its users?

Introducing a --dry-run flag to `gh pr create` will help people test their workflows/scripts without the need to do echos.

### Additional context

https://github.com/cli/cli/issues/1145 suggested raising a PR for this particular case.
comments: Hey @v1v thanks for creating this. As mentioned in #1145 we are open to adding `dry-run` to individual commands. Perhaps you can give a bit more detail about what you'd like to see as a result of providing `--dry-run` here? What kind of output would you want?

> what you'd like to see as a result of providing --dry-run here?

Sure, I'd like to see what parameters would be used if the PR was created.

> What kind of output would you want?

If I use the same output from https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/5098/files#diff-e15aeab65f4100441b2e8a9a3cdb63ebcaf971bb0b0c839cd790bb752a3ec35eR261

```Cucumber
Given a branch that has already been pushed to the origin
When `pr create --draft --fill-first --body 'my super-body' --dry-run --label external --label core --reviewer v1v`
Then the below output will be printed
Would have created a Pull Request with:
title:	feat: support dry-run in gh pr create
draft:	true
labels:	[external core]
reviewers:	[v1v]
--
my super-body
```

I just made a quick PR to support the above, see https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/8376

After thinking a bit more about this idea, I'd like to propose a similar output to the one when running `gh pr view`:

- https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/06e438b4b4a63ce1ad7486fb7e93091e35906451/pkg/cmd/pr/view/view.go#L139-L171
- https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/06e438b4b4a63ce1ad7486fb7e93091e35906451/pkg/cmd/pr/view/view.go#L180-L271


There are a few fields that won't be available, but overall it might help with having a similar UI experience.

What do you think?
I've just labelled this `help wanted` to indicate that we are happy to accept contributions for it, but I am aware you've already opened a PR for discussion @v1v 🚀

review_comments: As far as I can tell, the main difference between these two branches is the printing of the "draft" state, and the markdown rendering. Is the markdown rendering important enough to diverge here?

I used the same principles done in some other places, such as https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/8948ee8c3beaf432676061aaaf481d2f41039483/pkg/cmd/release/view/view.go#L118-L126

If tty, then https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/8948ee8c3beaf432676061aaaf481d2f41039483/pkg/cmd/release/view/view.go#L147-L149

Otherwise: https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/8948ee8c3beaf432676061aaaf481d2f41039483/pkg/cmd/release/view/view.go#L190-L193


IMO, I prefer the same output regardless of the command.
